title: Here Are Ghosts
text:
Title: Here Are Ghosts

In the great cities we see so little of the world, we drift into our minority. In the little towns and villages there 
are no minorities; people are not numerous enough. You must see the world there, perforce. Every man is himself a class; 
every hour carries its new challenge. When you pass the inn at the end of the village you leave your favorite whimsy behind you; 
for you will meet no one who can share it. We listen to eloquent speaking, read books and write them, settle all the affairs of the universe. 
The dumb village multitudes pass on unchanging; the feel of the spade in the hand is no different for all our talk: good seasons and bad 
follow each other as of old. The dumb multitudes are no more concerned with us than is the old horse peering through the rusty gate of the village 
pound. The ancient map-makers wrote across unexplored regions, “Here are lions.” Across the villages of fishermen and turners of the earth,
 so different are these from us, we can write but one line that is certain, “Here are ghosts.”
 W. B. Yeats, The Celtic Twilight: Faerie and Folklore
